title: Learning types
memoryHook: Labels teach, clusters discover, rewards steer.
facts: Supervised learning uses labeled examples.
Unsupervised learning discovers patterns in unlabeled data.
Reinforcement learning learns actions from rewards and penalties.
confusions: Classification predicts categories; regression predicts numeric values.

title: Classification metrics
memoryHook: Precision trusts alarms; recall finds cases.
facts: Precision is true positives divided by all predicted positives.
Recall is true positives divided by all actual positives.
F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
confusions: Prioritize precision when false alarms are costly; prioritize recall when missed positives are costly.

title: Inference patterns
memoryHook: Now: real-time. Later: batch. Long: async. Sporadic: serverless.
facts: Real-time endpoints serve low-latency interactive requests.
Batch inference processes offline collections.
Asynchronous inference queues large-payload or long-running requests.
Serverless inference fits intermittent traffic without capacity management.
confusions: Training learns parameters; inference uses the trained model.

title: Managed AI service compass
memoryHook: Read, see, hear, speak: Comprehend, Rekognition, Transcribe, Polly.
facts: Textract extracts text, forms, and tables from documents.
Comprehend analyzes language; Rekognition analyzes images and video.
Transcribe is speech-to-text; Polly is text-to-speech.
Lex builds conversational interfaces; Personalize builds recommendations.
confusions: Translate changes language; Transcribe changes speech into text.

title: Tokens, context, and embeddings
memoryHook: Tokens are pieces; context is the desk; embeddings are coordinates.
facts: Tokens are the units a language model processes and generates.
The context window limits the token span available in one interaction.
Embeddings represent semantic meaning as vectors.
confusions: Tokenization splits content; embedding maps meaning into vector space.

title: Generative AI tradeoffs
memoryHook: Capable is not factual, deterministic, cheap, or explainable.
facts: Hallucinations are plausible outputs that are unsupported or false.
Probabilistic token selection can make output nondeterministic.
Model selection balances capability, latency, cost, complexity, and compliance.
confusions: A fluent response is not proof of factual accuracy.

title: Agentic AI and MCP
memoryHook: An agent plans and acts; MCP gives tools a common plug.
facts: Agentic AI pursues goals through planning, memory, tool use, and workflow orchestration.
MCP standardizes how AI applications connect to external tools and context.
Context engineering assembles instructions, facts, tools, memory, and conversation state.
confusions: A chatbot that only returns text is not automatically an agent.

title: Current AWS GenAI tools
memoryHook: Bedrock builds, Quick works, Kiro codes, Strands wires, AgentCore runs.
facts: Amazon Bedrock provides managed foundation-model access.
Amazon Quick is an agentic workspace for business research, insight, and action.
Kiro supports specification-driven AI development.
Strands Agents is an SDK for agents; AgentCore provides production agent services.
confusions: SageMaker JumpStart supplies pre-trained models and solution templates; it is not the same as Bedrock managed FM APIs.

title: RAG versus fine-tuning
memoryHook: RAG supplies facts; fine-tuning shapes behavior.
facts: RAG retrieves relevant context at inference time without retraining the model.
Fine-tuning changes model behavior with task-specific examples.
Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock manages ingestion, retrieval, and grounded generation.
confusions: Use RAG for changing private knowledge; do not fine-tune merely to inject frequently changing facts.

title: Prompt patterns
memoryHook: Zero tells, few shows, chain decomposes, negative forbids.
facts: Zero-shot prompting gives instructions without examples.
Few-shot prompting includes a small number of examples.
Chain-of-thought prompting encourages intermediate reasoning.
Negative prompting states content or behavior to avoid.
confusions: In-context examples guide a request without changing model weights.

title: Generation controls
memoryHook: Temperature varies; top-p weighs mass; top-k counts choices.
facts: Lower temperature generally makes output more consistent.
Top-p samples from a cumulative probability mass.
Top-k restricts sampling to a fixed number of likely tokens.
confusions: These controls affect token selection, not the model context-window size.

title: Foundation model evaluation
memoryHook: ROUGE summarizes, BLEU translates, BERTScore means, humans judge nuance.
facts: ROUGE measures overlap for summarization.
BLEU compares machine translations with references.
BERTScore compares semantic similarity with contextual embeddings.
LLM-as-a-judge applies a rubric through another language model.
confusions: Automatic metrics should be paired with business metrics and human evaluation when quality is subjective.

title: Responsible AI
memoryHook: Fair, explainable, private, robust, controlled, truthful.
facts: Responsible AI includes fairness, explainability, privacy, robustness, controllability, veracity, and governance.
Governance establishes oversight, accountability, policies, and decision rights.
confusions: Responsible AI is a lifecycle practice, not a single model metric.

title: Transparency versus explainability
memoryHook: Transparency shows the system; explainability explains the outcome.
facts: Transparency communicates design, training, limitations, and intended use.
Explainability helps people understand model behavior or a prediction.
SageMaker Model Cards document model details; SageMaker Clarify analyzes bias and explanations.
confusions: A model card is documentation; a feature-attribution method explains prediction influence.

title: Human-centered oversight
memoryHook: Explain for the affected person, then give a path to respond.
facts: Human-centered explainability tailors explanations to stakeholder needs.
Human review is useful for high-impact or low-confidence decisions.
Feedback mechanisms help affected users question or correct outcomes.
confusions: Human oversight does not remove the need for automated evaluation and monitoring.

title: Security service compass
memoryHook: IAM grants, KMS keys, Macie finds, PrivateLink isolates.
facts: IAM controls identities and permissions; apply least privilege.
AWS KMS manages encryption keys.
Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3.
AWS PrivateLink enables private access through VPC endpoints.
confusions: Macie discovers sensitive S3 data; it does not grant access or manage encryption keys.

title: AI interaction defenses
memoryHook: Limit access, filter input, ground output, log the path.
facts: Prompt injection uses untrusted input to override intended behavior.
Bedrock Guardrails can filter denied topics, harmful content, and sensitive information.
RAG grounding, output validation, and confidence scoring help detect hallucinations.
confusions: Guardrails reduce risk but do not prove every generated claim is true.

title: Audit and governance services
memoryHook: CloudTrail events, Config state, Audit Manager evidence, Artifact reports.
facts: CloudTrail records API activity.
AWS Config records resource configuration and evaluates rules.
AWS Audit Manager collects evidence for assessments.
AWS Artifact provides AWS compliance reports and agreements.
confusions: CloudWatch provides operational metrics, logs, and alarms; CloudTrail records account and API events.

title: SSE-S3 versus SSE-KMS access
memoryHook: S3 key: GetObject. KMS key: GetObject plus Decrypt.
facts: A role needs S3 object permissions such as s3:GetObject to read an object.
SSE-S3 uses Amazon S3 managed keys and requires no separate KMS decrypt permission.
SSE-KMS access also requires the applicable KMS key permissions and key policy.
confusions: Do not add kms:Decrypt merely because an object is encrypted; first identify SSE-S3 versus SSE-KMS.
